summary: Two people come to beis din holding one garment, and each says he found it or that it is all his. Each one swears, and they split it; if one claims only half, they split it in a different way.
stIntro: The early commentaries ask why this chapter, which discusses details of the halakhot of found items, precedes the second chapter, which discusses the fundamental halakhot of found items. Tosafot explain that as tractate Bava Metzia follows tractate Bava Kamma, the halakhot of found items are elucidated in this chapter as a continuation of the topics discussed in the last chapter of Bava Kamma, which discussed the division of items between litigants by means of an oath, which is also the ruling in the mishna here (see Shita Mekubbetzet). The Rosh explains that because there is a suspicion of theft in this case, these matters are juxtaposed with the halakhot of theft, which are described at length in Bava Kamma.

chunks.explain: Each one is holding one side of it.
chunks.st: If two people came to court holding a garment,

chunks.en: This one says, "I found it!"
chunks.st: and this one, the first litigant, says: I found it,

chunks.en: And that one says, "I found it!"
chunks.st: and that one, the second litigant, says: I found it;

chunks.en: This one says, "All of it is mine!"
chunks.st: this one says: All of it is mine,

chunks.en: And that one says, "All of it is mine!"
chunks.st: and that one says: All of it is mine; how does the court adjudicate this case?

chunks.en: This one must swear that he owns
chunks.st: This one takes an oath that he does not have ownership of

chunks.en: no less than half of it.
chunks.st: less than half of it,

chunks.en: And that one must swear that he owns
chunks.st: and that one takes an oath that he does not have ownership of

chunks.en: no less than half of it, and they split it.
chunks.st: less than half of it, and they divide it.

chunks.en: If this one says, "All of it is mine,"
chunks.st: If this one says: All of it is mine,

chunks.en: and that one says, "Half of it is mine,"
chunks.st: and that one says: Half of it is mine,
chunks.stMore: since they both agree that half of the cloak belongs to one of them, the conflict between them is only about the other half.

chunks.en: the one who says, "All of it is mine"
chunks.st: Therefore, the one who says: All of it is mine,

chunks.en: must swear that he owns
chunks.st: takes an oath that he does not have ownership of

chunks.en: no less than three parts out of four.
chunks.st: less than three parts, i.e., three-fourths, of it,

chunks.en: And the one who says, "Half of it is mine"
chunks.st: and the one who says: Half of it is mine,

chunks.he: יִשָּׁבַע שֶׁאֵין לוֹ בָהּ פָּחוֹת מֵרְבִיעַ.
chunks.en: must swear that he owns no less than one quarter.
chunks.st: takes an oath that he does not have ownership of less than one-quarter of it.

chunks.en: This one takes three parts,
chunks.st: This one takes three parts,

chunks.en: and that one takes one quarter.
chunks.st: and that one takes one-quarter.

summary: Two people are riding on one animal, or one is riding and one is leading it, and each says it is all his. Each swears and they split it; if they agree or have witnesses, they split it with no oath.

chunks.he: הָיוּ שְׁנַיִם רוֹכְבִין עַל גַּבֵּי בְהֵמָה,
chunks.en: If two people were riding on the back of an animal,
chunks.st: If two people were sitting in a riding position on the back of an animal, e.g., a donkey or camel,

chunks.he: אוֹ שֶׁהָיָה אֶחָד רוֹכֵב וְאֶחָד מַנְהִיג,
chunks.en: or one was riding and one was leading it,
chunks.st: or one was sitting in a riding position on the animal and one was leading it by its halter,

chunks.en: and this one says, "All of it is mine!"
chunks.st: and this one says: All of it is mine,

chunks.en: and that one says, "All of it is mine!"
chunks.st: and that one says: All of it is mine, how does the court adjudicate this case?

chunks.en: This one must swear that he owns
chunks.st: This one takes an oath that he does not have ownership of

chunks.en: no less than half of it.
chunks.st: less than half of it,

chunks.en: And that one must swear that he owns
chunks.st: and that one takes an oath that he does not have ownership of

chunks.en: no less than half of it, and they split it.
chunks.st: less than half of it, and they divide it.

chunks.en: When they agree with each other
chunks.st: When they admit to the validity of each other’s claims

chunks.en: or when they have witnesses,
chunks.st: or when they each have witnesses attesting to their claims,

chunks.en: they split it without any oath.
chunks.st: they divide the disputed item without taking an oath,
chunks.stMore: as an oath is administered only in a case where the parties have no other way to prove their claims.

summary: A man riding an animal saw a lost object and told his friend to hand it to him. If the friend picked it up for himself, it is his; but once he gave it to the rider, he cannot change his mind.

chunks.en: If a man was riding on
chunks.st: If one was riding on

chunks.en: an animal and saw a lost object,
chunks.st: an animal and saw a found item,

chunks.en: and he said to his friend, "Give it to me!"
chunks.st: and said to another person who was walking beside him: Give it to me,

chunks.en: If the friend picked it up and said, "I got it for myself!"
chunks.explain: Picking it up is a way of getting it.
chunks.st: if the pedestrian took it and said: I have acquired it for myself,

chunks.en: then it is his.
chunks.st: he has acquired it by means of lifting it, even though he did not see it first.

chunks.en: But if after he gave it to the rider he said,
chunks.st: But if, after giving it to the one riding the animal, he said:

chunks.en: "I got it first for myself,"
chunks.st: I acquired it for myself at the outset,

chunks.en: his words mean nothing.
chunks.st: he has said nothing and the rider keeps the item.

summary: Just falling on a lost object does not make it yours; picking it up does. A person's field can get for him an animal that cannot run away, but not one that runs or flies off.

chunks.en: If a man saw a lost object and fell on it,
chunks.st: If one saw a found item and fell upon it,
chunks.stMore: intending to thereby acquire it, but did not employ one of the formal modes of acquisition,

chunks.en: and another man came and grabbed it,
chunks.st: and then another came and seized it,

chunks.en: the one who grabbed it gets it.
chunks.st: the one who seized it acquired it because he employed one of the formal modes of acquisition.

chunks.en: If a man saw people running after a lost animal,
chunks.st: If one saw people running after a found ownerless animal, e.g.,

chunks.en: like a deer with a broken leg,
chunks.st: after a deer crippled by a broken leg,

chunks.en: or baby birds that cannot fly yet,
chunks.st: or after young pigeons that have not yet learned to fly, which can be caught easily,

chunks.en: and he said, "My field should get it for me,"
chunks.explain: The animal was in his field.
chunks.st: and he said: My field has effected acquisition of this animal for me,

chunks.en: then his field gets it for him.
chunks.st: it has effected acquisition of it for him.

chunks.en: But if the deer was running the normal way,
chunks.st: If the deer were running in its usual manner,

chunks.en: or the baby birds were flying,
chunks.st: or the young pigeons were flying,

chunks.en: and he said, "My field should get it for me,"
chunks.st: and he said: My field has effected acquisition of this animal for me,

chunks.en: his words mean nothing.
chunks.st: he has said nothing,
chunks.stMore: as one’s courtyard cannot effect acquisition of an item that does not remain there on its own.

summary: Whatever a man's young children, his Canaanite servants or his wife find belongs to him. But what his grown children, his Jewish servants or his divorced wife find belongs to them.

chunks.en: What his young son and daughter find,
chunks.st: With regard to the found item of one’s minor son or daughter, i.e., an ownerless item that they found;

chunks.en: what his Canaanite servant and maid find,
chunks.st: the found item of his Canaanite slave or maidservant;

chunks.en: and what his wife finds,
chunks.st: and the found item of his wife,

chunks.en: all these belong to him.
chunks.st: they are his.

chunks.en: But what his grown son and daughter find,
chunks.st: By contrast, with regard to the found item of one’s adult son or daughter;

chunks.en: what his Jewish servant and maid find,
chunks.st: the found item of his Hebrew slave or maidservant;

chunks.en: and what his wife finds after he divorced her,
chunks.st: and the found item of his ex-wife, whom he divorced,

chunks.he: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא נָתַן כְּתֻבָּתָהּ,
chunks.en: even if he has not yet paid her kesubah,
chunks.explain: The kesubah is money a husband promises his wife.
chunks.st: even if he has not yet given her payment of the marriage contract that he owes her,

chunks.en: all these belong to them.
chunks.st: they are theirs.

summary: Someone found loan documents. Rabbi Meir says it depends on whether the document lets the lender collect from land that was sold; the Sages say he never gives them back.

chunks.en: If someone found loan documents,
chunks.st: With regard to one who found promissory notes,

chunks.en: if they say that the borrower's land is a guarantee,
chunks.explain: The lender may take land the borrower sold, to pay the loan.
chunks.st: if they include a property guarantee for the loan

chunks.en: he should not give them back,
chunks.st: he may not return them to the creditor,

chunks.en: because beis din would collect with them.
chunks.explain: Maybe the loan was already paid.
chunks.st: as, if he were to return them, the court would then use them to collect repayment
chunks.stMore: of the debts from land that belonged to the debtor at the time of the loan, even if that land was subsequently sold to others.

chunks.en: If they do not say the land is a guarantee,
chunks.st: If they do not include a property guarantee,

chunks.he: יַחֲזִיר, שֶׁאֵין בֵּית דִּין נִפְרָעִין מֵהֶן,
chunks.en: he gives them back, because beis din would not collect from sold land with them.
chunks.st: he returns them to the creditor, as in this case the court will not use them to collect repayment of the debt from purchasers of the debtor’s land.

chunks.en: These are the words of Rabbi Meir.
chunks.st: This is the statement of Rabbi Meir.

chunks.en: But the Sages say,
chunks.st: And the Rabbis say:

chunks.he: בֵּין כָּךְ וּבֵין כָּךְ לֹא יַחֲזִיר,
chunks.en: either way he should not give them back,
chunks.st: In both this case and that case he should not return the promissory notes to the creditor,

chunks.en: because beis din would collect with them.
chunks.st: as, if he were to return them, the court would in any event use them to collect repayment of the loan from purchasers of the debtor’s land.

summary: If someone finds a get, a document freeing a servant, a will, a gift document or a receipt, he does not give it back, because maybe the writer changed his mind and never meant to hand it over.

chunks.en: If someone found a get for a woman,
chunks.explain: A get is the paper a man gives to divorce his wife.
chunks.st: If one found bills of divorce,

chunks.en: or papers that set servants free,
chunks.st: or bills of manumission of slaves,

chunks.en: or wills, gift papers or receipts,
chunks.st: or wills, or deeds of a gift, or receipts,

chunks.en: he should not give it back,
chunks.st: he may not return these items to the one who is presumed to have lost them,

chunks.en: because I say they were written
chunks.st: as I say it is possible that they were written and then the writer

chunks.en: and then the writer changed his mind and decided not to give them.
chunks.st: reconsidered about them and decided not to deliver them.

summary: Some court papers that are found must be given back. Papers found in a bag or tied together go back too, and the mishnah says to whom; a paper whose story nobody knows stays put until Eliyahu comes.

chunks.en: If someone found papers of a court's pricing of land, or papers for food,
chunks.explain: Food papers: a promise to feed someone.
chunks.st: If one found documents of appraisal of a debtor’s property for the purpose of debt collection; or documents concerning food,
chunks.stMore: which were drawn up when one accepted upon himself to provide sustenance for another;

chunks.en: papers of chalitzah and of mi'un,
chunks.explain: These are court papers about ending a marriage tie.
chunks.st: documents of ḥalitza; or documents of refusal
chunks.stMore: of a girl upon reaching majority to remain married to the man to whom her mother or brothers married her as a minor after the death of her father;

chunks.en: or papers of choosing judges,
chunks.st: or documents of beirurin, a concept that will be explained in the Gemara;

chunks.en: or anything beis din did,
chunks.st: or any court enactment, e.g., a promissory note that has been authenticated by the court,

chunks.en: he must give it back.
chunks.st: in all of these cases, the finder must return the document to its presumed owner.

chunks.en: If he found papers in a bag or in a box,
chunks.st: If one found documents in a ḥafisa or in a deluskema, both of them types of containers, or if he found

chunks.en: a roll of papers,
chunks.st: a roll of documents

chunks.en: or a bundle of papers,
chunks.st: or a bundle of documents,

chunks.en: he must give them back.
chunks.st: he must return them.

chunks.en: And how many make a bundle of papers?
chunks.st: And how many documents are considered to be a bundle of documents? It is

chunks.en: Three tied together.
chunks.st: three that are tied together.

chunks.en: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says,
chunks.st: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: If the documents make reference to loans of

chunks.en: If they show one person who borrowed from three people,
chunks.st: one person who borrowed money from three people,

chunks.en: he gives them back to the borrower.
chunks.st: the finder must return them to the debtor,
chunks.stMore: as they were presumably in his possession before being lost. If the documents make reference to loans of

chunks.en: If three people borrowed from one person,
chunks.st: three people who borrowed money from one person,

chunks.en: he gives them back to the lender.
chunks.st: he must return them to the creditor, as they were presumably in his possession before being lost.

chunks.en: If someone found a paper among his papers
chunks.st: If one found a document among his documents that were given to him by other people as a trustee,

chunks.en: and he does not know what it is about,
chunks.st: and he does not know what its nature is,
chunks.stMore: i.e., he does not remember who gave it to him or whether the debt mentioned in it has been paid,

chunks.en: it should stay put until Eliyahu comes.
chunks.explain: Eliyahu HaNavi will tell us what to do with it.
chunks.st: the document is placed aside until Elijah the prophet comes and clarifies the issue through his prophecy.

chunks.en: If there are notes of cancelling with them,
chunks.st: If there are cancellations of contracts [simponot] among them,

chunks.en: he should do what the notes say.
chunks.st: he should do what is stated in the simponot.
